news.headline: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
news.summary: Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN&nbsp;human rights chief&nbsp;Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

news.headline: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
news.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

news.headline: Protecting the storytellers: Women journalists on the frontline of conflict
news.summary: As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.&nbsp;

news.headline: DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000
news.summary: As Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) surpass the 10,000 mark, the World Health Organization (WHO) has underlined the need for continued efforts to contain spread of the disease.&nbsp;

news.headline: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
news.summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.&nbsp;

news.headline: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
news.summary: The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 28 October, Member States will vote for the 34th time on a resolution calling for it to end.

news.headline: Gaza: Families brace for fourth winter in tents as aid operations remain stymied
news.summary: Families in Gaza are bracing for a fourth winter in tents and makeshift shelters as UN aid operations face mounting obstacles, with transport suspended on Tuesday due to Israel’s closure of the key Kerem Shalom crossing for election day.&nbsp;

news.headline: Security Council LIVE: Women and girls face greater dangers in war
news.summary: From Gaza to Yemen, women and girls are facing ever greater dangers this year simply surviving in war zones. The Security Council meets Tuesday to debate the best way to improve security for women caught up in conflict.

news.headline: World News in Brief: ‘No safe place in Ukraine’, IAEA calls for Iran nuclear inspections, Kenya hosts thousands of Ethiopians fleeing clashes
news.summary: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) on Tuesday urged continued international support for Ukraine’s population as Russian airstrikes intensify and humanitarian needs grow in advance of another bitterly cold winter.

news.headline: Ebola: 20 contacts released from quarantine in Kenya, amid vaccine ‘hope’ in DR Congo
news.summary: Twenty people associated with Kenya’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease have been reunited with their families after being released from quarantine following completion of a mandatory 21-day monitoring period.&nbsp;

news.headline: World News in Brief: Ethiopians flee to Kenya amidst renewed conflict, new head of UN’s food programme, UN mission in Somalia concludes
news.summary: Around 36,600 people have fled into northern Kenya following an uptick in fighting on the Ethiopian side of the border.&nbsp;

news.headline: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
news.summary: War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.&nbsp;

news.headline: Ukraine: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
news.summary: Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine&nbsp;said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

news.headline: In Egypt, Guterres warns against Iran-US escalation
news.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war between Iran and the United States in remarks on Monday to journalists in Cairo, Egypt.&nbsp;

news.headline: West Bank: Hebron crackdown displaces thousands, Türk warns of ethnic cleansing
news.summary: Israel’s “aggressive operation” in the West Bank city of Hebron raises serious concerns of ethnic cleansing, UN human rights chief Volker Türk warned on Monday, as the number of Palestinians forced from their homes passed 3,000 on the eve of Israeli elections.

news.headline: Ebola: UN officials condemn killing of nurse in DR Congo
news.summary: The UN’s Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) have deplored the killing of a nurse working to halt the spread of the disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).&nbsp;

news.headline: World News in Brief: Iran nuclear inspections, deadly church attack in Jordan, El Fasher – one year on
news.summary: The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, called on Friday for a swift return of inspectors to Iran, warning of growing fragility in the global nuclear non-proliferation regime.

news.headline: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
news.summary: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.

news.headline: Sudan: Drone strikes killed at least 306 people in three weeks
news.summary: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Friday strongly condemned an escalation in drone strikes across Sudan this month, which killed at least 306 people and injured hundreds more in the first three weeks of October alone.

news.headline: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
news.summary: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.

news.headline: Soil mapping aims to boost agricultural production in Kenya
news.summary: A new Kenyan initiative is helping farmers better understand their soils in a bid to improve crop yields amid intensifying climate shocks.

news.headline: ‘Burden and loss’ builds in DR Congo, as Kenya strengthens Ebola containment
news.summary: As Ebola continues to spread in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), more resources are needed to fight the disease and feed patients and families, UN agencies said on Friday.

news.headline: DR Congo: Ebola responders under pressure as outbreak expands
news.summary: As the deadly Ebola disease outbreak reached an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), investigators pursued all leads on Thursday to assess the risk of the disease spreading in Nigeria.

news.headline: First human case of Shamonda virus reported in France as patient dies
news.summary: A patient in France has died after being infected with Shamonda virus, the first recorded human case of the disease.

news.headline: ‘Ominous start’ to West Bank olive harvest amid settler attacks
news.summary: The use of&nbsp;live ammunition, arson and the destruction of centuries-old olive trees have marked the opening weeks of this year’s harvest in the occupied West Bank.

news.headline: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
news.summary: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.&nbsp;

news.headline: WHO supports Nigeria after first Ebola case confirmed
news.summary: The World Health Organization (WHO) is assisting Nigeria following confirmation of the first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease in the country.

news.headline: Migrants paid up to $500 million in smuggling fees on European sea routes
news.summary: The price tag for smuggling on European sea routes reached up to half a billion dollars last year, the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) and the UN migration office, IOM, reported on Wednesday.
